smell: runDeploy checks deployYes before deployDryRun and returns after saving the config, so `okdctl deploy --yes --dry-run` silently skips the dry-run preview the user asked for. --yes is documented as 'skip prompts, use defaults' and --dry-run as 'preview terraform plan and step listing without deploying' — the combination should still preview, not no-op into a config save.
severity_reason: Behavior-divergence-from-help-text: user asked for a preview, got a config save. Not user-harming (no mutation), but the flag pair silently does the wrong thing — failure to meet the documented contract.
fix_summary: Reorder the guard: if deployDryRun { return runDeployDryRun(ctx, cfg) } BEFORE the deployYes short-circuit, or gate the --yes fast-path on !deployDryRun. Matches runDestroy (destroy.go:71-73) which checks destroyDryRun first. ~3 LOC, plus a deploy_test.go case asserting --yes --dry-run exits via the plan preview.
rule_source: clig.dev §Flags: 'Flags should compose; combining two non-mutually-exclusive flags should produce the union of behaviors, not the union of first-wins'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/destroy.go:71-73 checks destroyDryRun before destroyForce
must_preserve: --yes fast-path must still skip the interactive wizard when --dry-run is not set.

smell: Generated CLI reference for `okdctl destroy` is stale: commit afsd79b added --skip-terraform, --skip-cleanup, --skip-firewall to destroy.go, but docs/cli/okdctl_destroy.md still lists only --confirm-cluster, --dry-run, -h/--help, --keep-isos, -y/--yes. CI's docs-drift check (.github/workflows/ci.yml: `git diff --quiet docs/cli/`) would fail on this state.
fix_summary: Run `make docs` (or `go run ./cmd/okdctl-gen-docs`) and commit docs/cli/. The regenerator is already in CI (.github/workflows/ci.yml:65); the drift is pre-commit residue from the afsd79b work. Zero code change.
rule_source: Repo convention: README.md §Release checklist 'regenerate the CLI reference and commit any drift'
must_preserve: docs/cli/ content shape (cobra auto-gen output) — only regenerate, do not hand-edit.

smell: docs/cli/json-schema.md documents field shapes that do not match what the code emits. `okdctl status --format=json` is documented with cluster_name/version/ready_nodes/total_nodes but emits api_reachable/nodes/degraded_operators/addons. `okdctl releases list --format=json` is documented as {series:[{minor,latest,versions[]}]} but emits a flat array of OKDVersion with a release_type int. Consumers pinning on the documented shape break on first call.
severity_reason: Documented user-facing contract is false. Scripts written against docs/cli/json-schema.md will ship broken and we have no test catching the divergence. Adjacent-rubric anchor: silent behavior divergence from what the docs promise.
fix_summary: Option (a, preferred): update docs/cli/json-schema.md to match code — for status enumerate api_reachable, nodes[{name,role,ready}], degraded_operators, addons[{name,healthy,error?}]; for releases list enumerate the flat OKDVersion array including release_type (int, document the 0-4 encoding or switch code to emit the string label). Add fixture-based golden tests (status_test.go, releases_test.go) that compare marshaled output against the doc so future drift fails CI. Option (b): reshape code to match docs (bigger — changes user-visible JSON). Pick (a); the code already shipped.
rule_source: clig.dev §Machine-readable output: 'A documented schema that does not match reality is worse than no schema'
repo-counter-example: internal/distribution/okd/releases/types.go:26-35 pins JSON tags and flags this file as the stability anchor — docs must follow.
must_preserve: JSON struct tags on clusterStatus / nodeStatusEntry / OKDVersion are the shipped contract — fix the doc, not the keys.

smell: runDescribeAddon emits JSON with a hyphen-cased key `display-name` while every other field in the same payload and every other JSON endpoint uses snake_case (api_reachable, ready_nodes, degraded_operators, release_date, release_type). jq consumers have to quote the field: `jq '."display-name"'`, which is a pain-point.
evidence:
lines := []struct{ k, v string }{
    {"name", info.Name},
    {"display-name", info.DisplayName},  // <-- hyphen
    {"description", info.Description},
    {"category", info.Category},
    {"health", health},
}
fix_summary: Rename the JSON key to display_name in the lines slice when describeFormat == outputJSON. Text mode can keep the hyphenated label (it is human-facing and reads as a single phrase). Or split into two slices: textLines uses `display-name`, jsonPayload uses `display_name`. Update docs/cli/json-schema.md to match. Backward compat: this field was shipped once — document the rename in CHANGELOG or emit both keys for one release.
rule_source: clig.dev §Machine-readable output: 'Pick one key convention and stick with it'
repo-counter-example: every other json:"…" tag in the codebase (OKDVersion, clusterStatus, addonStatusEntry) uses snake_case
must_preserve: Text-mode output of describe-addon can keep the hyphenated label; it's the JSON key that breaks consistency.

smell: completionCmd.Use is 'completion [bash|zsh|fish|powershell]' — square brackets per man(1) convention mean optional, but cobra.ExactArgs(1) rejects zero-arg. The shell token is required; Use should render `<bash|zsh|fish|powershell>`.
fix_summary: Change Use to 'completion <bash|zsh|fish|powershell>'. Same pattern as internal/cli/addon.go:67 ('uninstall <name>') and releases.go:53 ('show <version>'). Zero behavior change; one-line edit.
must_preserve: ValidArgs list and Args validator must stay — only the Use string changes.

smell: cleanupCmd has no --dry-run flag while its destructive siblings (deploy, destroy, update-ingress) all do. cleanup removes packages, dnsmasq/haproxy configs, ignition files, and terraform state — destructive enough that a preview flag has the same value proposition. Asymmetric surface across the destructive-verb family.
fix_summary: Add cleanupDryRun bool and --dry-run flag. Branch to a runCleanupDryRun before the confirmation prompt; enumerate what would be removed (work directory path, haproxy config block, dnsmasq drop-in path, packages to uninstall) via the existing cleanup.Options struct — do not call cleanup.Execute. ~20 LOC matching the update_ingress.go:46-59 shape.
rule_source: clig.dev §Destructive ops: 'every destructive verb should support --dry-run'
repo-counter-example: internal/cli/destroy.go:54 and internal/cli/update_ingress.go:43 — sibling commands both have --dry-run
must_preserve: cleanup.Options and cleanup.Execute semantics must stay.

smell: addon install/uninstall and describe-addon gained ValidArgsFunction for tab-completion; releasesShowCmd still has none. Tab-completing `okdctl releases show <TAB>` does filesystem completion instead of version suggestions. Catalog fetch is network-bound, which was likely the hesitation — but the local disk cache (internal/distribution/okd/releases/cache.go) is cheap enough to prime completion in the common case.
fix_summary: Add ValidArgsFunction that reads the disk cache (releases.NewOKDVersionFetcher has a cache-backed path) and returns Versions + ShellCompDirectiveNoFileComp. Fall through to ShellCompDirectiveError when the cache is empty rather than fetching on tab — keeps completion latency under the 1s shell threshold. ~15 LOC. Supersedes the addon-args portion of the 2026-04-20 finding; addon commands were fixed.
rule_source: Cobra docs §Custom completions: 'Use ValidArgsFunction to supply completion at runtime'
must_preserve: ExactArgs validator must stay; completion augments, does not replace.

smell: exitCodeFor maps ConfigError=2 (not EX_DATAERR=65 or EX_CONFIG=78), NetworkError=3 (not EX_UNAVAILABLE=69), ClusterError=4 (not EX_UNAVAILABLE=69), AuthError=5 (not EX_NOPERM=77). The taxonomy IS published at the package doc (root.go:1-8). Choice is consistent with itself but deviates from BSD sysexits.h that CI/scripts might expect. Unchanged from 2026-04-20 audit; open question whether the tradeoff is correct.
fix_summary: Keep the current mapping for backward compatibility (scripts may pin 2/3/4/5); add a regression test in root_test.go asserting each typed error reaches the right code, and --version / help exit 0. Optionally introduce --exit-code-mode={compat|sysexits} for opt-in BSD mapping. Not a behavior-break finding; keep as an open question until scripts pin explicit codes.
rule_source: BSD sysexits.h: EX_USAGE=64, EX_DATAERR=65, EX_UNAVAILABLE=69, EX_NOPERM=77, EX_CONFIG=78
clig.dev §Exit codes: 'Follow a convention or document yours'
must_preserve: ConfigError=2 / NetworkError=3 / ClusterError=4 / AuthError=5 / 64 for flag errors / 130-143 for signals must stay; these are shipped.

smell: main() calls preflight() before cli.Execute(); signal.Notify setup lives inside internal/cli/root.go:execute(). If the user hits Ctrl-C during preflight's euid check, OKDCTL_BIN_DIR validation, or PATH mutation, the process dies with SIGINT default (no partial summary, undocumented behavior). preflight is sub-millisecond in practice, so this is a robustness nit not a live bug. Unchanged from 2026-04-20 audit.
fix_summary: Either (a) accept current behavior (document in main's package comment: 'preflight runs before signal setup; it is small enough that interruption is racy but not harmful') or (b) move signal.Notify earlier into main() and pass ctx through preflight. Only pay for (b) if preflight grows (e.g. adds a network probe).
rule_source: clig.dev §Signals: 'Handle SIGINT at the earliest reasonable point'
must_preserve: preflight's 'refuse root' check must remain in main so it runs before cobra.
